label: Person
name: Johann IV. von Dražice
summary:
John IV of Dražice (1300-1343) was a pivotal figure in the Luxembourg dynasty's ascension to the Bohemian throne, shaping the course of Czech history.

He served as the penultimate Bishop of Prague from 1301 to 1343, a period marked by significant cultural and architectural developments. As a patron of the arts, John IV supported notable architects and artists, leaving a lasting legacy in the city's landscape.

The impact of his tenure can still be seen in the enduring influence of the Luxembourg dynasty on Czech politics and society, as well as the rich cultural heritage it left behind.

'For our kingdom to prosper, we must strengthen our ties with God, through prayer, pilgrimage, and service,' John IV once said, encapsulating the spiritual essence of his era.
